metadata.goal: Analyze individual mobility patterns across activity purposes and spatial contexts.
metadata.category: Single-user routine regularity, discretionary mode flexibility, distance-mode structure, and center-suburban speed context
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 15 Single-user Routine, Mode, and Speed Context
metadata.dataset_description: One user's work and discretionary trajectories with purpose, transport mode, distance, recurring route geometry, and timestamped point speeds labelled by center, transition, or suburban spatial context.
metadata.metric_note: `spatial_area` is a point-level city-context label; `avg_point_speed_kmh` is the mean of point speeds over a trajectory.

insights: Work-related trips exhibit highly regular departure times and recurrent spatial patterns, forming the most stable component of the user's mobility routine.
The user shows substantially greater mode flexibility for shopping, dining, and leisure trips than for recurrent work trips.
Short discretionary trips involve multiple transport modes, whereas longer trips converge toward the smaller set of motor-vehicle and public-transit modes.
The user's point speeds are lower in the center area and higher in suburban areas for every transportation mode.
summary: This user's work travel is the most temporally and spatially regular activity. Shopping, dining, and leisure use a broader range of modes; short discretionary trips are multimodal, whereas longer ones use motor vehicle or public transit. Point speeds are consistently lower in center contexts across modes.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
